lines: Daniel is two books in one. Chapters one to six are stories of Daniel and three friends, taken from Judah to serve the king of Babylon.
Chapters seven to twelve are visions of empires, and of the kingdom of God that outlasts them all.

scripture.text: To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding

lines: Chapter one is in Hebrew. Chapters two to seven are in Aramaic, framed by two visions of four kingdoms followed by God's kingdom.
Then the book returns to Hebrew: the ram and the goat, a prayer, and a final vision.

scripture.text: the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the Most High rules
lines: Every chapter presses one claim. God gives kingdoms and takes them away. Proud kings are made to confess it.
The Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind.
Empires are real and dangerous. But they're temporary, and they answer to a higher throne.

scripture.text: the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind

chapters.kicker: Watch for: faith that will not bow
lines: Daniel and his friends learn Babylon's language and serve its kings with integrity. But they draw the line at worship.
Three of them won't bow to the golden statue. They trust God to save them, and they trust him even if he doesn't.
But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods.

scripture.text: But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods

lines: When a decree forbids prayer, Daniel keeps praying at his open window, just as he had done before.
He's put into the lions' den and brought out alive. And a foreign king confesses that God's kingdom will not be destroyed.

scripture.text: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: one like a son of man
lines: In the visions, empires rise like beasts from the sea. And one like a son of man is given a kingdom that will not pass away.
Jesus took that title for himself.

scripture.text: I saw One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven.

lines: Many read the four kingdoms as Babylon, Media-Persia, Greece, and Rome. Many others read them as Babylon, Media, Persia, and Greece. Careful readers also differ on when the book was finished.
The visions are pictures, not a code for the news. The book's own concern is endurance and hope.
Start with chapter one. The key chapters are two, three, four, six, seven, nine, and twelve.
Empires rise and empires pass. The Most High rules.
